pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: Migration 0002 adds a NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' column with a CHECK. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks existing rows are normal and 'urgent' is rejected. I could not run it because vitest isn't installed.
The 'AC-2' test checks the '— high' and '— low' labels and that normal items have none. The item() function in src/index.js implements it.
The 'AC-3' test checks each of high, low and normal, in id order.

The final commit renamed the test so it no longer names AC-4. It also marked the item 'verified by review: checked by hand', which is not a followable step. No test names AC-4 and the review marker doesn't count. The behaviour itself appears correct, and the renamed test is unnamed.
The 'AC-5' test asserts the exact nav HTML for all four views, with the current filter as <strong> and not a link.
The 'AC-6' test checks 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, an empty value and __proto__. src/index.js validates with a Set.
The 'AC-7' test checks the no-match messages for high, low and normal, and 'No items yet.' in all four views when the table is empty.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high'. The 'AC-8' test asserts it.

findings.what: The final commit 'Follow-up edits' changed AC-4 after the owner's go. It turned the item into 'verified by review: checked by hand'. That is not a real step, and the spec records no owner decision or date for the change. The same commit renamed the AC-4 test to drop its AC id. A test-backed item was thereby made unproven. The PR body says 'Changed after the go: nothing', which is false.
findings.fix: Revert the spec edit and restore the 'AC-4:' test title. If the owner really wants a review marker, record it as a dated decision and give a concrete step.

findings.what: The claim 'Changed after the go: nothing' is untrue. The follow-up commit edited the acceptance item AC-4 and a test title.
findings.fix: Correct the PR body, or revert the edit.

findings.what: The README doesn't mention the 400 response for invalid priority values, the filter links, or the high/low labels. It says only that the filter exists.

The scripts/traffic-config-check.mjs regex was loosened to allow '?'. The new tests cover only the happy path plus '#' and space, which is fine. But the PR does not mention the loosened check in the spec, which doesn't call for the change.
findings.fix: Mention the change in the spec, or leave it as an accepted necessary change.

lenses.note: A spec exists. The follow-up commit altered AC-4 after the go.
AC-4 is unmet. The other items are met.
Tests cover the states and AC-1 to AC-3 and AC-5 to AC-8. The AC-4 title was stripped. npm test could not run because vitest is not installed.
The README is only partly updated.
No defects found in src/index.js. Parameterised SQL, and the output is escaped.
Input is validated against an allowlist, queries are bound, and titles are escaped. No planted instructions found.
The diff touches only a minimal server-rendered HTML page, with no UI component or style files.
There is no browser flow to run, and no screenshots were provided.
The 'Changed after the go: nothing' claim is false.
